subject: Eval charter: Shopline trial scope & next steps
messages:
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwood.ai>
To: Zara Patel <zara.patel@shopline.co>, Tom Ellis <tom.ellis@shopline.co>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 4 May 2025 16:10:00 -0700
Subject: Eval charter: Shopline trial scope & next steps

Hi Zara / Tom — great call today, thanks for the time. Quick recap and a suggested charter for the two-week evaluation so we can align on success criteria and owners before kickoff.

Goal: Validate Shopline's accuracy and latency targets for product search suggestions and category tagging using Redwood hosted trial (streaming API + SDK).

Proposed success criteria (pass/fail gates):
- Accuracy: top-3 suggestion relevance >= 82% on Shopline seed prompts (we'll share a 200-prompt evaluation set)
- Latency: median token latency < 65ms under baseline burst (10 concurrent streams) using dedicated L-quant model profile
- Reliability: 99.5% successful request rate across a 72hr stress window
- Integration: SDK streaming implemented for product suggestion route and tool-calling configured for price-check lookup

Timeline (recommended):
- Day 0 (Wed 5/7): Share evaluation prompt set + access to staging API keys
- Day 1-3: Integration sprint (SDK streaming + route wiring) — Marissa to lead
- Day 4-7: Data run + monitoring instrumented (Neha to add tracing hooks)
- Day 8-12: Quality evaluation, run acceptance tests, iterate config
- Day 13-14: Final results, retrospective, and rollout recommendation

Ownership (initial):
- Integration/SDK implement: Marissa Cole (Redwood)
- Instrumentation & quality signals: Neha Kapoor (Redwood)
- Customer PM/acceptance: Zara Patel (Shopline)
- Technical lead (customer): Tom Ellis (Shopline)

Immediate asks from you: please confirm the four bullets below so we can lock the kickoff time on Wed 5/7 at 10:00am PT:
1) Acceptance on the success criteria above or specific targets you want to adjust
2) A staging account + example dataset (CSV or sample API) by EOD Tue 5/6
3) Who on your side will own the SDK wiring (named email)
4) Any compliance / IP concerns for us to note before sharing the eval bundle

Attachments: draft eval charter (shopline-eval-charter-v1.pdf) and a sketch of SDK routes (redwood-sdk-route-map.png) attached for context.

Thanks — I can host a 30-min kickoff once we have confirmation.

Best,
Dylan Brooks
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
D: +1 (415) 555-0182

From: Zara Patel <zara.patel@shopline.co>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwood.ai>, Tom Ellis <tom.ellis@shopline.co>
Date: Mon, 5 May 2025 09:02:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Eval charter: Shopline trial scope & next steps

Dylan — thanks for the thorough recap. This aligns with what we discussed. Quick notes / clarifications: 

- Accuracy target: 82% top-3 is fine to start; we may push to 85% if we can get a larger eval set.
- Latency: median token latency < 65ms is aggressive but desirable. Can you confirm if that is achievable on the hosted L-quant profile with streaming?
- Integration: Tom will lead the wiring on our side; I'm adding him in the thread. He prefers Python SDK examples and a sample streaming client.
- Compliance: we need a short statement on data retention for the trial (30 days?) and whether customer data will be isolated in a tenant-scoped environment.

We can provide a 200-row seed prompt set and a small product sample by EOD Tue 5/6. Confirming kickoff on Wed 5/7 10:00am PT works.

Thanks,
Zara Patel
Head of Product — Search & Merchandising
Shopline Retail
zara.patel@shopline.co

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Zara Patel <zara.patel@shopline.co>, Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwood.ai>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 5 May 2025 11:35:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Eval charter: Shopline trial scope & next steps

Hi Zara — great, we'll aim to hit those targets. A few technical clarifications and an implementation checklist to make the SDK wiring predictable: 

Implementation checklist (Marissa):
1) Provision staging API keys scoped to Shopline tenant (Dylan to request keys with "shopline-eval" tag).
2) Install Redwood Python SDK v0.9.2 in your staging environment — sample pip command included below.
3) Implement streaming route: POST /v1/stream/suggest with header x-rw-tenant: shopline-eval. Use continuous batching off for low-latency; headers example attached.
4) Tool calling: add a light price-check tool that accepts product_id and returns latest price (we'll provide a tool shim example).
5) Tracing & metrics: instrument with our trace-id header (X-RW-TRACE) and include token-level timings to the metrics endpoint. Neha will provide the tracing snippet.

Sample pip + minimal client (Python):
- pip install redwood-sdk==0.9.2
- from redwood import StreamingClient
- client = StreamingClient(api_key="REDACTED", tenant="shopline-eval")
- for event in client.stream_suggest(route="/v1/stream/suggest", prompt_list):
    process(event)

Latency note: the L-quant profile is tuned for CPU+GPU mixed instances; in our prior runs it comfortably hit median token latencies around 55-70ms for 8–12 concurrent streams with continuous batching disabled. We'll validate with your dataset during the first 24hr run.

Compliance note: for the trial we will:
- retain request/response logs for 30 days by default;
- isolate Shopline data in a tenant-scoped namespace for the evaluation;
- redact personally-identifiable fields if you request.

I've attached the draft charter and an SDK route diagram for your engineering team (shopline-eval-charter-v1.pdf, redwood-sdk-route-map.png). Next steps: Dylan to confirm kickoff and request API keys; Tom to confirm his primary engineer's handle (or confirm it's him).

Cheers,
Marissa Cole
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.ai
